instantiated_cells.justification: The statute requires registered principals—not lobbyists—to file the periodic expense statement, so there is no separate lobbyist-filed spending report.
Although semiannual expense statements are required, the required filer is the principal, not the lobbyist, so the lobbyist does not have a semiannual spending report obligation.
No provision requires a lobbyist to file an annual spending report; the periodic reporting duty is imposed on principals.
The only periodic expense statement cadence specified is July 31 and January 31 for principals, not quarterly lobbyist reports.
The statute does not require lobbyists to file monthly spending reports; reporting is by principals on semiannual dates.
No triannual lobbyist spending report is required; the statute specifies semiannual principal expense statements.
The statute does not create any other lobbyist-filed periodic spending report cadence; instead it imposes semiannual expense statement filing on principals.
Periodic expense statements are required of principals on July 31 and January 31, and the statute does not require any periodic spending report to be filed by lobbyists themselves.
The aggregate total of lobbying expenditures is reported in the principal’s expense statement, not in a lobbyist-filed spending report.
Compensation to lobbyists is included in the principal’s aggregate lobbying expenditures, but the statute does not require lobbyists to file a spending report disclosing their compensation.

The statute requires principals to file the expense statement and to file lobbyist-provided information as an attachment, but it does not impose on lobbyists a duty to file a report breaking down compensation by payer.
Any itemization requirements in Wisconsin attach to the principal’s expense statement, not to a lobbyist’s own spending report.
The statute does not require lobbyists to file an itemized spending report; the required report is the principal’s expense statement.
Expense categories are part of the principal’s expense statement content, and no lobbyist-filed spending report exists to categorize expenses.

While the law restricts furnishing things of value and requires principals to report certain reimbursements, it does not require lobbyists to file a spending report disclosing gifts/entertainment/transport/lodging.
Indirect lobbying costs are reported in the principal’s expense statement, not via a lobbyist-filed periodic spending report.

Identification of legislative proposals and proposed administrative rules is a principal reporting duty, and the statute does not require lobbyists to file a spending report including such identifiers.
Reporting legislative proposal numbers is imposed on principals as a condition of authorizing lobbying, not on lobbyists through a spending report.
The principal’s report must identify proposals/topics but the statute does not require any lobbyist-filed spending report to disclose a position on bills.
General topics/issues are reported by principals when identifying lobbying topics, and there is no separate lobbyist spending report requiring issue disclosure.
Subject-matter/topic reporting is required of principals, not of lobbyists in a periodic spending report.
Principals report time proportions for topics (and aggregate expenditures), but the statute does not require lobbyists to file a spending report allocating expenditures per issue.
The daily itemization of time spent meeting with officials is part of the principal’s expense statement, and no lobbyist-filed spending report requires disclosure of contacts made.
Lobbyists provide identifying information on a license application, but the statute does not require lobbyists to file a periodic spending report containing their address/phone.
Because Wisconsin does not require lobbyists to file periodic spending reports, it does not require such a report to list principal names.
Principal contact information is part of principal registration and filings, not a lobbyist-filed spending report (which the statute does not require).
Nature of the principal’s business/purpose is required in the principal’s registration statement, not in a lobbyist-filed periodic spending report.
The statute imposes periodic expense statement filing on principals, and it does not create a lobbyist spending report obligation (including a 'no activity' report) for lobbyists.
There is no lobbyist-filed spending report and thus no report scope requiring disclosure of spending benefiting household members of officials.

unscoreable_emissions.justification: Because there is no lobbyist-filed spending report required, there is no 'other' cadence to specify.
